close_reason: Fixed in commit d0a0bd4. metadata_set now carries an # Errors rustdoc section explaining the ClientError::InvalidArgument path on serde_json::to_value failure for the update map. Documents that the wire request is streamed without a cap and recommends batching for thousands-of-patches workloads. No defensive-cap added — matches canonical mail-client (email_set), which also lets the caller decide the budget.
description:
src/methods/metadata.rs:144-148 — metadata_set serializes the update HashMap<Id, PatchObject>:

    args[\"update\"] = serde_json::to_value(&u).map_err(|e| {
        jmap_base_client::ClientError::InvalidArgument(format!(
            \"metadata_set: serializing update map failed: {e}\"
        ))
    })?;

This handles serde_json::to_value failure correctly. But the doc-comment does not state:
- Whether there is a maximum number of updates per call. The server caps it (RFC 8620 §5.3 'maxObjectsInSet'), but this crate doesn't validate against that cap client-side.
- That over-large maps will incur a server-side 'requestTooLarge' (RFC 8620 §3.6.2) error rather than a typed local error.
- That serde_json::to_value cannot fail for HashMap<Id, PatchObject> in practice (both Id and PatchObject are infallible-Serialize), but the .map_err is defensive and the error message is never reached in real code.

This is a minor docs-as-contract gap. Two reads:
1. The defensive .map_err path is unreachable; document why it exists.
2. The doc-comment should reference maxObjectsInSet so callers know about the cap.

Marked opinion: low engineering value, but the dead error-handling branch is mildly confusing if a future maintainer asks 'when does this fire?' and the answer is 'never under any realistic input'. Could be replaced with .expect with a Serialize-infallibility note, matching the destroy/Id Vec idiom three lines below.

Workspace-wide: same shape on email_set.
title: metadata_set: no documented panic / error path for over-large 'update' HashMap
